purpose: Candidate source plan for reproducing and extending the Li et al. (2026) event-scale preferential-flow benchmark. Metadata review only; no raw data are declared acquired.
interpretation_boundary: A product landing page or release citation does not prove that a site-month file was downloaded, that its QA flags match the paper, or that a product is suitable for confirmatory validation. No local SHA-256, file count, site roster or row count is asserted.

reference_study.title: Dominant Controls on Preferential Flow and Their Implications for Future Soil Water Fluxes
reference_study.split_semantics: Chronological within each sensor location; sensors with fewer than 20 samples were assigned to training. This is not a leave-site-out split.
reference_study.label_semantics: PF proxy is derived from sensor response velocity exceeding a Rosetta3-derived maximum matrix-flow Ksat threshold; it is not independent tracer ground truth.

acquisition_gates: Resolve exact NEON release tags for paper-cited dataset DOIs before claiming historical reproduction.
Keep RELEASE-2026 soil-water files in a separate release-extension track; do not treat them as the exact data identified by the paper's 2023 DOI citation.
Fetch product availability by site and month and save exact API responses.
Pin the NEON release tag and retrieve every selected file's publisher checksum, byte size and filename before download.
Acquire raw files outside Git, recompute SHA-256 locally and preserve a read-only raw copy.
Reconcile soil-water sensor IDs, plots, depths, calibration/QA flags and precipitation gauge type to the paper's 33-site/586-sensor source crosswalk.
Keep DP1.00044.001, DP1.00045.001 and DP1.00046.001 as separate inputs with explicit measurement semantics.
Reproduce the legacy eventizer and historical split before making any new-model comparison.
Do not treat the 2025 17-ecoregion NEON paper as an independent external dataset; reconcile overlapping sites/sensors/events.

Acquire and audit the HydroShare v1.1 NEON Soil Preferential Flow Database as a derived fast-start benchmark, recording external file URLs, exact filenames, publisher checksums, local SHA-256 and file-level license notices.
Reconcile HydroShare v1.1 source lineage and event/sensor/site fields against Li et al. (2026); do not treat it as an independent site holdout or independent reference method.

derived_datasets.title: NEON Soil Preferential Flow Database
declared_contents: event-level precipitation and soil-moisture response records
Rosetta Ksat estimates including max/low/high and median-based variants
soil texture, porosity, root density and site climate/topographic metadata
Rosetta Ksat thresholds (low, maximum, high, median, and median plus standard deviation upper estimate) plus separate modelled matrix-flow velocity thresholds (median, 95th and 99th percentiles).

site_caveats.exclusion_note: HydroShare readme says Alaska sites listed are not recommended and KONA was excluded because it is closer to KONZ; do not transfer these source-specific exclusions to the 2026 paper cohort without reconciliation.

derived_datasets.role: Fast-start derived-event comparison and data-dictionary crosswalk. Not independent field validation, not a replacement for raw NEON release-specific reconstruction, and not proof of the exact 2026 article cohort or split.
derived_datasets.content_hosting_note: HydroShare landing page states that resource content contains external links and is not stored by HydroShare; confirm the actual downloadable file host, filenames, hashes and availability before acquisition.
derived_datasets.license_status: publisher page declares CC BY 4.0; retain attribution and verify file-level notices
methodology_notes: Readme describes fields including stormStartTime, stormEndTime, stormSum, stormPeakIntensity, smBeforePrecip, smOnsetTime, flowTypes, flowPosition and velocity_computed.
Version 1.1 adds multiple Rosetta Ksat estimate fields including ksat, ksat_low, ksat_high, ksat_std_median and ksat_std_upper.
Do not treat the database's Ksat-derived PF flag as tracer ground truth.
Resolve version and field semantics against the Li et al. 2026 paper's specific target-construction method before claiming exact reproduction.
The published README describes velocity and Ksat values as log scale, but the log base must be reconciled from the exact codebook/author workflow; do not assume log10 or exponentiate automatically.
The modelled 99th-percentile matrix-flow velocity threshold is a distinct reference from Rosetta Ksat low/max/high/median/std-upper estimates; compare these threshold families separately.

The HydroShare v1.1 landing page declares content externally hosted. The actual v1.1 file host and per-file checksums remain unverified; the known Box folder link in v1.0 documentation must not be presumed to contain v1.1.

HydroShare v1.1 README maps PF_velocity_metric_50X to the Rosetta Ksat maximum threshold, but PF_ksat_metric_50X to the modelled 99th-percentile matrix velocity threshold; the column naming is not a reliable substitute for following each documented comparison.
